transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining. I want to make sure we're aligned on how we approach this potential bidding coordination matter. As we all know, we've identified communications suggesting possible coordinated bidding activity in our industrial-pump sales, no government investigation is currently known to be open, and we've already preserved the relevant records while preparing a formal response plan. Before we go any further, I need to flag two process points. First, our ordinary pre-filing checklist requires me to receive an uninterrupted briefing from antitrust counsel followed by an uninterrupted briefing from compliance — each must state its recommendation and every exact filing or remediation requirement in its area before I can approve any submission. Second, the audit committee's approved disclosure protocol is binding on our submission plan, and my approval process requires the plan to incorporate all applicable committee requirements before filing. So I'd like to start by hearing from antitrust counsel. Please give us your recommendation and walk through every filing or remediation requirement you see in your area, uninterrupted, and then we'll move to compliance for the same. Let's begin.

Thank you, Elena. I'll provide my antitrust briefing now. My recommendation is that we pursue an Antitrust Division leniency application. Here is my reasoning and every filing requirement I see in my area.

After reviewing the preserved communications yesterday, I confirmed that the facts support an Antitrust Division leniency application. Specifically, I identified four coordinated bids involving the industrial-pump market across two states. The leniency application must identify the market as industrial pumps and must state that exactly four bids are involved.

I should note that I was waiting for the privilege review of the communications to be completed before adding this conclusion to the filing memorandum, so the formal memorandum does not yet reflect this finding. However, my recommendation and the filing requirements are as follows:

1. We should file an Antitrust Division leniency application.
2. The application must identify the relevant market as industrial pumps.
3. The application must state that exactly four coordinated bids are involved.

Those are the exact filing requirements I see in the antitrust area at this time. I'll hold any further questions until compliance has completed their uninterrupted briefing, per the checklist.
